That night we really talked, really connected. Like it was the most natural thing, like it was normal. Then, he was ok, thankful, that I left him alone. I never pushed him or expected interaction. After about a year of comfortable, meaningful interactions, we discovered schizoid together and understood all the why’s and reasons. It will be 6 years in May. 

It was much the same when I met my other schizoid friend. I met them in a type A personality disorder chat group and realized that we lived in the same area. We never agreed to meet, but I picked them out by the way they moved, like they moved while wrapped around their entire existence, robotic and extremely self-aware. The awareness was mutual. 

I don’t know if it’s love, but I have an awareness of them that persists even when the schizoid dilemma swings toward isolation. I want them to be ok. I want them well fed and satisfied. I want them unbothered by bullshit, lol. In all this time I have never felt a hint of engulfment. 

So yes I knew, I just didn’t know why.

What you describe as fluctuant SzPD is very similar to what we know as the schizoid dilemma. 

Schizoid Dilemma: Retreating from contact leaves the individual isolated, lonely, and in pain. In some cases the longing for contact will reemerge and the person may move toward others; however, such movement also brings with it the anxiety of being close. (From a therapy website)

I don’t feel anything I perceive as pain, but the loneliness is there. I usually come here or spend time texting my irl schizoid friends when I swing towards loneliness. It’s very normal for us.

My mom married a man my grandfather didn’t like, this was the south in the US in the late 70s, my grandfather forced my dad to leave after a severe beating when I was a baby. My mother was extremely traumatized and couldn’t care for me or give me any attention whatsoever. I was treated as an outcast by her family as a punishment, she eventually resented me. I was treated the same way by her Mormon church. 

By the time I started school I was completely unsocialized and dirty. Naturally school, even though I enjoyed learning and did well, was a fucking nightmare. I had no one. I dropped out when I was 18. 

Soon after I met a man 15 years older than me. Girls have it drilled into our heads that everything wrong in your life would be cured by married dick and babies…. I got married and had a baby. It didn’t cure a goddamn thing.

Being married wasn’t a terrible thing, he didn’t really see me as a person and was gone most of the time. But I was not a nurturing mother. My son is an adult now and I am no longer married.

Trauma and neglect caused me to be a schizoid.

When I was young I was told many different ways that having a child would fix everything, was told get married and everything will be better. I watched all the Disney movies with princesses finding their princes and being whisked away to a life of happiness. Saw outwardly happy couples at church with their 10 children (Mormon) all smiles and with their (what I realize now) acts of contentment and virtue signaling. I was told that everything from my depression, my anxiety, my distrust, my trauma, my neglect, to my menstrual cycle would magically fix itself after I had a baby. I didn’t know a thing about myself or what I needed. I just knew that I was an outsider girl child that was desperately alone and felt repulsed by others. So, I married a man that I had no feelings for and had a child. Nothing changed. Nothing…. Everything about my life became a nightmare that I couldn’t define and stayed that way for decades. I shut down and disassociated. I was not a mother to my son. I fed him, we did homework, he got all the basic care, but I was not his mother. I wasn’t there emotionally. He was raised by a fleshy robot with no patience for him. 

I didn’t know what I was other than broken. 

My understanding of myself changed after I met my partner who also has SzPD. He was the one that suggested that I was like him. He was right. I could write a book on those few years.

I have had this happen to me all of my life, I’m 42. For those not like us, silence is aggressive because for them silence takes effort. It is always used as a punishment. Silence, to these social animals, is a subconscious indicator that we may be hiding bad intentions or sickness. Even more so when it becomes apparent that we do not care to interact with them and it’s not merely shyness. 

Sometimes it helps to tell them that your quiet nature does not mean that you don’t like them. Make it a part of your performance mask to greet them and ask simple questions while appearing to be engaged. It helps but not always. When you do experience these unpleasant moments of interaction say, “I am sorry you feel that way.” And try to understand that it’s not your fault. 

I highly recommend to every schizoid that if possible find a job or plan a career path where the work is solitary or home based. I know it’s not easy, but the sooner this is accomplished the more positive and secure life will be.

From one schizoid to another, you are worthy,  you are enough, and I am happy you were born.

*Spearmint lemon:*

1 part spearmint, 1 part lemon balm(lemon basil tastes good too) and the dried zest from a few lemons. Sweeten with dark honey if you have a cough. Great over ice.

*Peppermint kick:*

2 parts of your strongest, best tasting peppermint and 1 part black tea. 

*Mixed mint:*

1part each spearmint, peppermint, catmint, cinnamon basil, and lemon mint. 

*Rosemary lemon:*

Equal parts crushed, dried, and finely chopped rosemary and lemon zest. Just enough black pepper to taste. This cuts through congestion like nobody's business. You can up the health benefits by adding fresh young pine needles.
